exposure: COVID-19 vaccination status during pregnancy (at least one dose vs. no doses)
outcome: COVID-19 vaccine adverse events (AEs) (e.g., malaise, headaches, chest pain, breathing problems, sleep problems)
pregnancy complications (e.g., abortions, miscarriage, oligohydramnios, abnormal placentas, preterm labor)
fetal complications (e.g., abnormal fetal growth, birth defects)
cohort: The cohort consisted of 438 women in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, who had recently given birth or were pregnant within the previous 8 weeks.
finding: The study found that while COVID-19 vaccination during pregnancy significantly reduced post-vaccination COVID-19 rates, vaccinated women experienced higher rates of several adverse events and pregnancy/fetal complications (e.g., abortions, abnormal fetal growth, oligohydramnios) compared to unvaccinated women.
